text: For Zion's sake I will not keep silent, for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until her righteousness breaks out like the dawn and her salvation blazes like a torch.
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow.

versions.text: The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory; and you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb יִקֳּבֶנּוּ means to designate or pronounce a name; "bestow" or "designate" captures the sense better than the generic "give," and reads well aloud.

text: You will be a crown of beauty in the LORD's hand, a royal diadem in the palm of your God.

No longer will you be called Forsaken, and no longer will your land be called Desolate; but you will be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married—for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
As a young man marries a virgin, so your sons will marry you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
On your walls, Jerusalem, I have posted watchmen; all day and all night they will never be silent. You who remind the LORD, take no rest for yourselves,

versions.text: On your walls, Jerusalem, I have posted watchmen; all day and all night they will never be silent. You who call on the LORD, give yourselves no rest,
versions.explanation: הַמַּזְכִּרִים אֶת־יְהוָה means "those who cause the LORD to remember" / "who remind the LORD" (i.e., bring his promises before him), not "call on the LORD." The participle governs the LORD as object.

text: and give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth.

The LORD has sworn by his right hand and by his mighty arm: "Never again will I give your grain to your enemies for food, and never again will foreigners drink the new wine for which you have labored.
But those who harvest the grain will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather the grapes will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.

versions.text: But those who harvest it will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather the grapes will drink the wine in my holy courts."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses pronominal suffixes referring back to the grain and new wine of v. 8; "drink it" preserves that link. "Courts of my sanctuary" renders חַצְרוֹת קָדְשִׁי more precisely, and the parallel with the first clause is clearer.

text: Pass through, pass through the gates! Clear the way for the people! Build up, build up the highway! Remove the stones! Raise a banner for the nations!
See, the LORD has proclaimed to the ends of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion, "See, your salvation comes! See, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him."

versions.text: See, the LORD has proclaimed to the ends of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion, "See, your salvation comes! See, his reward is with him, and his recompense goes before him."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no verb in the final clause; the added "goes" is unnecessary and breaks the tight parallel of "with him ... before him."

text: They will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD; and you will be called Sought After, a City No Longer Forsaken.
